Ambiguous? "view a list of sponsors" fairly clear. Could interpret list content? Not materially different maybe. No violation. Evidence empty.

BC-002: "view a list of user profiles" clear. No.

Ambiguous terms? "email all trainers at once from website" clear enough? Could be training coordinators need compose email? "for info and updates" maybe unclear purpose but not requirement ambiguity. No material different interpretations? Maybe "all trainers" all at once; okay. No violation.

BC-004: "As a attendee, I want to have a very clear map where the buildings and rooms are, so that I can make it to class on time."
Ambiguous? "very clear map" subjective, vague. Does it allow materially different interpretations? "very clear" quality ambiguous but requirement for map where buildings and rooms are. Could be subjective, but maybe not materially different requirements? It could mean interactive map, static map, detailed map. The phrase "very clear map where buildings and rooms are" is vague; but likely no materially different interpretation? Hmm criterion says vague terms allowing materially different requirements. "very clear map" is subjective but requirement is map with building/room locations. Could be satisfied in multiple ways, but requirements ambiguity? It doesn't specify format: map could be static image, interactive. That's underspecified maybe materially different. But should we flag? Need apply consistently. Many stories have vague nouns. But criterion asks avoid terms or abstractions leading to multiple materially different interpretations. BC-004 "very clear map" is a vague quality, but not term that leads to materially different? It might: "very clear" could mean high-resolution, indoor floor plans, wayfinding directions. Ambiguity in what constitutes map. Could be violation. But perhaps don't over-flag vague adjectives? Need decide. The definition says "avoids terms or abstractions that lead to multiple materially different interpretations." "very clear map" could be subjective but perhaps not leading to multiple materially different requirement interpretations? Hmm.

Need compare with full backlog? Individual. Could check if "map" defined? Not in backlog. But BC-004 itself ambiguous enough? Possibly moderate. Need binary. We need maybe flag clear ambiguities.

The sentence is malformed, ambiguity whether editing includes linking slides. "training node" could mean their training content. This can lead to materially different scope. Violation: vague "edit my training node" and "links to slides" unclear. Yes.
